subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Laminar vs. Turbulent Flow
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Laminar vs. Turbulent Flow.

hook.text: Open a faucet slowly — smooth stream. Open it wide — chaotic spray.

buildup.text: Smooth flow is laminar. Fluid moves in parallel layers with no mixing.

discovery.text: Above a critical speed, layers break apart into swirling turbulent eddies.

twist.text: Turbulence wastes energy as drag, but it also mixes fuel and air in engines.

climax.text: The Reynolds number predicts the switch. Below 2300, laminar. Above, turbulent.

punchline.text: Order or chaos — one number tells you which one wins.

quiz.question: What does the Reynolds number predict?
options: How fast a fluid can flow through a pipe
Whether flow will be smooth (laminar) or chaotic (turbulent)
The pressure drop across a valve
